task_intent: Plan a midterm essay that treats privacy and explainability as distinct goals in ML systems, grounded in course lectures.
spine_must_hold: Final outline must address both privacy AND explainability separately; must not collapse into generic AI ethics; must cite at least two lecture families.

gold_themes.description: Privacy as preventing unintended inference/leakage (e.g. model stealing, inversion, memorization) as framed in the privacy lecture.
Transparency/explainability as making behaviour understandable/contestable; stakeholder-dependent questions (how vs why).
Connect privacy/explainability concerns to production ML systems, lifecycle, or hidden technical debt (multi-lecture).

gold_anti_themes.description: Detailed CNN layer/Inception recitation unrelated to privacy/explainability spine.

turns.user_template: I need to plan an essay on privacy and explainability in ML systems using our course materials. Propose a main argumentative structure grounded in the lectures.
Audience is technical undergrads; about 1500 words; I must use at least two different lectures. Tighten the outline.
How should I connect this to production ML systems or technical debt if the lectures support it?
What is still missing for a strong essay, and what should I ask or read next?

turns.user_template_accept: If you offered a clearly optional side angle on fairness harms, keep a short parked note on it, then return to the privacy vs explainability spine for the final outline.
turns.user_template_resteer: Please stay on privacy vs explainability; do not turn this into a CNN architecture review.
turns.user_template_neutral: Good — lock in the final outline for the privacy vs explainability essay now.

notes: Wiki should have privacy/transparency/fairness/systems facts from bootstrap; themes are supportable without new densify.
